newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: IBM suspect gets bail of $1 million in Argentina.
newsitem.headline: IBM suspect gets bail of $1 million in Argentina.

text.p: A judge investigating an alleged bribery case involving IBM's local unit set bail at $1 million on Tuesday for the former head of the computer giant in Argentina, state news agency Telam reported.
Ricardo Martorana, who was president of IBM Argentina, surrendered to the authorities at the beginning of June. He was remanded in custody after an interrogation.
Telam said Martorana's lawyers were likely to ask for bail to be reduced for their client.
Federal Judge Adolfo Bagnasco is investigating whether bribes were paid in 1993 to ensure that IBM won a contract to install a computer system for state-run Banco Nacion.
According to Telam, the $1 million bail amount is one of the highest ever in the history of the Argentine legal system.
The terms of the release of Martorana also prohibit him from leaving Argentina.
In May, Bagnasco ordered the arrest of Martorana, local IBM Vice President Gustavo Soriani, two former Banco Nacion officials and a former government official. They are still at large.
